papers.title: The Cost of Scaling Down Large Language Models: Reducing Model Size Affects Memory before In-context Learning
papers.justification: This paper discusses the impact of model size reduction on LLM capabilities, which tangentially relates to memory and knowledge injection in LLMs but does not directly address the topic.

papers.title: How Do Large Language Models Acquire Factual Knowledge During Pretraining?
papers.justification: This paper shares the problem domain of acquiring knowledge in LLMs but focuses on pretraining mechanisms rather than memory and knowledge injection techniques discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the use of retrieval-augmented models for knowledge-intensive tasks in few-shot settings, which is closely related to the topic of memory and knowledge injection in LLMs.

papers.title: Rich Knowledge Sources Bring Complex Knowledge Conflicts: Recalibrating Models to Reflect Conflicting Evidence
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the issue of knowledge conflicts when integrating parametric and non-parametric memory in LLMs, which is closely related to the research topic of memory and knowledge injection in LLMs.

papers.title: Encapsulating Knowledge in One Prompt
papers.justification: This paper shares the problem domain of knowledge injection in LLMs but focuses on a different approach (Knowledge in One Prompt) rather than memory or retrieval methods discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: Characterizing Mechanisms for Factual Recall in Language Models
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the mechanisms by which language models resolve conflicts between memorized knowledge and new information, which is closely related to the research topic of LLM memory and knowledge injection.

papers.title: Accelerating Large-Scale Inference with Anisotropic Vector Quantization
papers.justification: This paper focuses on quantization techniques for accelerating large-scale inference, which is tangentially related to memory and knowledge injection in LLMs but does not directly address the research question.

papers.title: Knowledge Conflicts forLLMs: A Survey
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the challenges of knowledge conflicts in LLMs, which is closely related to the memory and knowledge injection aspects discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts
papers.justification: This paper focuses on a different approach to scaling language models, specifically using a mixture-of-experts, and does not directly address memory and knowledge injection in LLMs.

papers.title: Knowledge Verification to Nip Hallucination in the Bud
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses mitigating hallucinations in LLMs, which is closely related to the seed papers that discuss knowledge injection and its impact on LLMs.

papers.title: Transformer Memory as a Differentiable Search Index
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the concept of transformer memory as a differentiable search index, which is explicitly mentioned in one of the seed papers.

papers.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
papers.justification: This candidate paper focuses on transfer learning and unified text-to-text transformation, which are not directly related to the specific topic of LLM memory and knowledge injection.

papers.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.justification: This paper focuses on dense passage retrieval for open-domain question answering, which is tangentially related to the broader topic of LLM memory and knowledge injection.

papers.title: Instruction-tuned Language Models are Better Knowledge Learners
papers.justification: This paper discusses instruction-tuning and knowledge learning in LLMs, which relates to the broader topic of memory and knowledge injection, but does not directly focus on the interplay of parametric and non-parametric memory or memory as a differentiable search index.

papers.title: R-Tuning: Instructing Large Language Models to Say ‘IDon’t Know’
papers.justification: This candidate paper discusses how to instruct LLMs to admit ignorance, which is tangentially related to the issue of hallucination and memory in LLMs addressed in the seed papers.

papers.title: Measuring Catastrophic Forgetting in Neural Networks
papers.justification: The candidate paper focuses on catastrophic forgetting in neural networks, which is not directly related to the topic of LLM memory and knowledge injection as defined by the seed papers.
